properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive hashing library of the Ethereum dev toolchain: elliptic@6.6.1 uses it as its hash backbone and @ethersproject/sha2/@ethersproject/signing-key@5.8.0 (ethers v5, pinned in the lockfile) use it for SHA-2. The build ships it; the repo's own TS/Solidity code never imports it directly (verified by repo-wide grep). Quantum-unsafe hash family but Grover-only, so the D rating's low urgency is correct.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is THE Ethereum signature curve: ethers signs every message/typed-data in this repo (src/permit.ts permit helpers, all test signers) with secp256k1 ECDSA through this library, mirroring the first-party Solidity ECDSA library in contracts/libraries/ECDSA.sol that calls EVM precompile 0x1. The native secp256k1@4.0.5 binding is also pinned (yarn.lock:5851) via ethereumjs-util → ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3. Migration to ML-DSA is constrained by the EVM protocol (precompile 0x1 is fixed), n

properties.value: Live secp256k1 ECDSA at the core of this package: the 200 test/contracts/ECDSA.test.ts sites (page 1 sampled — uniformly ecdsa.recover / recoverOrIsValidSignature / recoverOrIsValidSignature_v_r_s calls) exercise the shipped contracts/libraries/ECDSA.sol, which verifies signatures via the ecrecover precompile (staticcall 0x1) for EIP-2612/Dai/USDC permits and ERC-1271; the yarn.lock site is the ECDSA capability of @openzeppelin/contracts 5.6.1 / ethers 6.17. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 provided by @noble/curves@1.2.0, declared in yarn.lock as a transitive dependency of ethereum-cryptography -> @metamask/eth-sig-util@9.0.0 (direct dep, used by src/permit.ts for EIP-712 domain hashing). Shipped in the dependency tree; no direct call site in application code — presence is the question here. Shor-vulnerable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped library: @noble/curves@1.2.0 ships P-256 (secp256r1) alongside secp256k1. No P-256 call site in the repo's own code — no direct @noble/curves import, no OpenZeppelin P256Verification usage (grep found only a 'secp256k1n' comment). Presence is the inventory fact here; the library is part of the published build via ethers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped library: in this tree elliptic is used by the ethers v5 path for secp256k1 ECDSA point math; no ECDH key-agreement call site exists in first-party code. Changeable only by bumping the @ethersproject/secp256k1 toolchain pins. Retroactively breakable primitive if ECDH were used, so its B- rating stands on availability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped library: the repo's first-party code touches only eth-sig-util's TypedDataUtils (EIP-712 hashing, src/permit.ts:77); X25519 has no call site here — tweetnacl arrives as eth-sig-util's internal dependency. Changeable only by @metamask/eth-sig-util dropping tweetnacl.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: keccak256 (Ethereum's pre-SHA-3 padding variant) confined to test code: ECDSA message hashing (ECDSA.test.ts:29,967,977), CREATE3 salt derivation (utils.test.ts:228,252,280), transient storage slot derivation (Transient.test.ts:184). Grover-only exposure (no Shor impact); salts/slots are non-security derivations. Low urgency; kept as part of the hash inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 via pbkdf2@3.1.6 plus @ethersproject/pbkdf2@5.8.0 (ethers-v5 tree, used by hdnode/json-wallets for mnemonic and Ethereum V3 keystore KDFs), all declared in yarn.lock. No application call site; dependency inventory. Password KDF — not Shor-relevant, Grover square-root only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 via @noble/hashes@1.3.2 (deps of @metamask/scure-bip39@2.1.1 and @metamask/utils@11.12.1, under @metamask/eth-sig-util@9.0.0); sha.js serves the same role for @ethersproject/sha2@5.8.0. Declared in yarn.lock; no app call site. Hash — Grover-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 attributed to @noble/hashes@1.3.2, which is genuinely declared in yarn.lock (via @metamask/scure-bip39 / @metamask/utils -> @metamask/eth-sig-util@9.0.0). The module list of that exact version could not be re-verified from the tree (no node_modules shipped), so the attribution is kept with that caveat. Hash — Grover-only; lowest urgency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The password-based KDF behind encrypted JSON keystores in the ethers v5 toolchain (and ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3's keystore path). No direct scrypt call in first-party code; the cost parameters (N/r/p) are chosen inside node_modules callers, so no parameter site exists in this repo to judge. Not Shor-vulnerable (memory-hard KDF); rated A- for a reason.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes provides keccak256 (Keccak/SHA-3) — the hash behind Ethereum addresses, transaction hashes and EIP-712 typed-data digests — exercised pervasively through ethers in this repo (src/permit.ts domainSeparator, every signTypedData digest). Also used by @metamask/scure-bip39@2.1.1 (~1.3.2, resolving to 1.3.3). Keccak is not Shor-broken; Grover-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM via @noble/ciphers@1.2.1, declared in yarn.lock as a transitive dependency of ethereum-cryptography -> @metamask/eth-sig-util@9.0.0 (yarn.lock:1160). @noble/ciphers 1.2.1 does ship AES-GCM. No app call site; dependency inventory. AEAD — quantum exposure limited to Grover key-size halving, not Shor-broken.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the one place in the toolchain where a PQ-safe AEAD protects real secrets: hardhat-keystore encrypts deployment-account keystores with ChaCha20-Poly1305 (password KDF from @noble/hashes@1.7.1, pinned line 1358). The plugin ships in this build; no keystore configuration was found in this repo's own hardhat config, but the capability and algorithm are present. Changeable only by hardhat's keystore version pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped library: tweetnacl's secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305) has no call site in first-party code — it ships as eth-sig-util's internal dependency. Symmetric AEAD, PQ-safe; A+ rating appropriate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@1.0.3 declared in yarn.lock:1127 as a direct dependency of @metamask/eth-sig-util@9.0.0 (the project's own direct dependency). tweetnacl ships Ed25519 signing, X25519 key exchange, XSalsa20-Poly1305 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD — the quantum-vulnerable asymmetrics arrive in the build through it. No direct application call site; dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 declared in yarn.lock:683 as a dependency of @ethersproject/json-wallets@5.8.0 (Ethereum V3 keystore password KDF); ethers-v5 tree pulled in by the Hardhat toolchain. No app call site; dependency inventory. Memory-hard KDF — not Shor-relevant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.12 declared in yarn.lock as the dependency of @ethersproject/sha2@5.8.0 (pure-JS SHA-256/SHA-512); ethers-v5 tree. No app call site; dependency inventory. Grover-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Classic elliptic-curve library in the ethers v5 toolchain path and behind the native secp256k1 binding (secp256k1 ECDSA point math). No direct import in first-party code, but the build ships it and its elliptic-curve implementations are reachable through the toolchain. Same logical pin as ALG-c9ffc8a8 (ECDH) — both describe this package's algorithm surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.3.2 / ^1.3.1 declared in yarn.lock:1134,1150 (dependencies of @metamask/scure-bip39@2.1.1 and @metamask/utils@11.12.1, both under @metamask/eth-sig-util@9.0.0). Provides SHA-2/SHA-3/Keccak/BLAKE2/RIPEMD160/scrypt/PBKDF2 — the hash layer of the Metamask sig-util chain. No app call site; dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 declared in yarn.lock:769,781 as a dependency of @ethersproject/sha2@5.8.0 and @ethersproject/signing-key@5.8.0 (which also pulls elliptic@6.6.1 — pure-JS secp256k1 ECDSA); ethers-v5 tree. No app call site; dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The curve library behind every ethers signing operation in this repo: Wallet/Signer.signTypedData and signMessage reach secp256k1 ECDSA through this package (see also ALG-92b28f71 secp256k1 and ALG-a6da3577 P-256, which describe its algorithm surface). Changeable only by bumping the ethers pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 seed/keystore derivation path of the Ethereum toolchain: pulled by ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 (via ethereumjs-util@7.1.5, a direct dependency); @ethersproject/pbkdf2@5.8.0 is separately pinned (yarn.lock:705). No direct PBKDF2 call or iteration-count choice exists in first-party code — parameters are set inside node_modules callers, so no CWE-916 iteration site is judgeable from this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ships the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD used to encrypt Hardhat keystores of deployment accounts (see ALG-c57b2423). PQ-safe symmetric crypto present in the build; changeable only by the hardhat-keystore pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: src/utils.ts:445 — getEthPrice() fetches the Coinbase spot price via global fetch (Node/undici default TLS settings); the only HTTPS client in the tree. Node version is unpinned in this repo (no engines field, .nvmrc or Dockerfile), so the negotiated key exchange is undecidable: Node >= 24.5.0 offers X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid by default; older Node defaults to classical ECDHE (X25519/P-256) — harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure, though the payload is public price data and the session is test-suppo
